title: Divide and Conquer: Region Self-Paced Physics-Informed Neural Networks

problem.claim: Physics-Informed Neural Networks suffer from the Unbalanced Prediction Problem, in which challenging regions are learned worse than smooth regions.

gap.claim: Coupling sample selection with difficulty evaluation can cause Difficulty Cohesion, weakening easy-to-hard curricula and limiting PINN learning efficiency.

contributions.claim: A divide-and-conquer framework for time-dependent PDEs partitions the temporal domain into subdomains and evaluates sample difficulty independently using PDE residual gradients.
A rank-based normalization strategy preserves relative easy-to-hard ordering and improves difficulty discrimination.
A bimodal self-paced scheduler converts ranked difficulty into smooth sample weights for progressively shifting attention from easy to hard samples.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on six PDE benchmarks reportedly improve prediction accuracy in challenging regions, maintain competitive overall performance, and incur practical computational cost.

narrative_sequence.summary: PINNs show potential for scientific computing and engineering simulation.
PINNs face unbalanced learning across regions, while existing adaptive and cognitive strategies can produce cohesive difficulty scores that weaken curricula.
RSPINNs partitions temporal domains, evaluates regional difficulty, normalizes rankings, and applies self-paced weighting.
The authors report results across six PDE benchmarks with improved challenging-region accuracy, competitive overall performance, and practical computational cost.

source_observation.claim: Difficulty evaluation may become less discriminative when sample selection and difficulty estimation are tightly coupled.

interpretation.claim: Separating difficulty assessment by region can help preserve distinctions among samples with different local learning difficulty.

application.claim: For spatially or temporally heterogeneous scientific models, evaluate curriculum difficulty within meaningful subdomains before assigning global priorities.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether regional difficulty evaluation is beneficial for domains without comparable temporal heterogeneity.

unknowns: The six PDE benchmarks and their characteristics are not specified.
Quantitative accuracy improvements, baselines, ablations, and computational-cost measurements are not provided.
The abstract does not report implementation, reproducibility, or failure-case details.
